# ansible-doc: fix indent and line wrapping for first line of (sub-)option and (sub-)return value descriptions

## Summary

ansible-doc uses a wrong indent for the first line of description of sub-options and sub-return values, and also does not wrap the first line of all option and return value descriptions correctly (as it only wraps the remainder of the first line, and wrapping doesn't know about the beginning).

Ref: https://github.com/ansible-collections/community.general/pull/9651#issuecomment-2632451897

Example: `ansible-doc -t inventory ansible.builtin.constructed`

Before:
```
           trailing_separator          Set this option to `false' to omit the `keyed_groups[].separator' after the h>
                               variable when the value is an empty string.
                               This option is mutually exclusive with
                               `keyed_groups[].default_value'.
```
You can see that the first line is indented much more than the others, and that the line overflows - you need to scroll to the right to see everything.

After:
```
           trailing_separator  Set this option to `false' to omit the
                               `keyed_groups[].separator' after the host variable when the
                               value is an empty string.
                               This option is mutually exclusive with
                               `keyed_groups[].default_value'.
```

## Issue Type

Bugfix Pull Request

# Add AnsiballZ debugging support with debugpy

## Summary

Adds support for debugging AnsiballZ modules with debugpy which is used by VSCode as its Python debugger DAP. Debugging can either be done through a manual Debugpy listening server through a launch.json configuration or through the new ansible-test --dev-debug-on-deman argument.

The `ansible-test` integration requires a change in debugpy that is not currently in a public release. It can be used by cloning the debugpy repo or waiting until the next release.

# add tech preview play argument spec validation

## Summary

Play argument spec validation runs after the play-level fact gathering.

The validate_argspec keyword supports templating for parity with the gather_* keywords. It can be a bool or argument spec string.

The task is tagged always, and is skippable since it inherits play tags.

Undocumented variables are ignored by default. module_defaults can define the optional argument "provided_arguments" to ensure there's documentation for arbitrary options. This provides flexibility and is the same mechanism supporting play-level fact gathering configuration.

When validate_argspec is set to True:
  - A play name is required.
  
When validate_argspec is True or an argument spec:
  - A file in the playbook directory matching the pattern {playbook}.meta{ext?} is required.
  - The playbook meta file must contain a dictionary containing an argument spec in the format:

```yaml
argument_specs:
  Play Name:
    options: {}
 ```

# Fix ansible-doc -l/-F/--metadata-dump for relative imports in filter/test plugins

## Summary

Fixes #85754.

ansible-doc supports getting the documentation for filter/test plugins in sub-directories, but fails when listing them if any contain relative imports.

I don't see any tests for sidecar documentation for filter/test plugins in a sub-directory (just [this]( https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/stable-2.19/test/integration/targets/ansible-doc/runme.sh#L88) and [this](https://github.com/ansible/ansible/blob/stable-2.19/test/integration/targets/collections/posix.yml#L139)), so I added one for that too.
